highlights.title: Apple Watch Series 12, Ultra 4 have wearables' “most accurate heart rate sensing"
highlights.summary: Apple announced the Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 today. Both include a new "Health Sensing System" and S11 chip that Apple claimed during its fall event today give the devices the “most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable." Both watches will use the new S11 chip alongside the new "Health…
body: The Health Sensing System includes redesigned photodiodes organized in a ring to capture light more efficiently and a larger electrode surface area for better skin contact. Additionally, the green LEDs on each Watch’s optical heart sensor are supposed to be bigger and more power-efficient and measure the user’s heart rate every 5 seconds. Users will be able to view their heart rate in real time with a new heart rate watch face special feature (also known as a complication ).

The new Watches can take HRV measurements up to 24 times more frequently than their predecessors, Apple said. HRV is an indicator of how well the body is able to adapt to changes such as stress and exercise.

“Overnight vitals now includes recovery HRV measurements analyzed against a user’s personal baseline, providing a more complete view of their health status. A new daytime vitals view lets users toggle between overnight and daytime metrics, and can potentially spot shifts in their metrics before they show up overnight,” Apple said in a press release.

highlights.title: Paul Christiano joins OpenAI Foundation Board
highlights.summary: Paul Christiano joins the OpenAI Foundation Board and its Safety and Security Committee, bringing experience in AI alignment, safety, and standards.
body: We’re announcing the appointment of Paul Christiano to the OpenAI Foundation Board. He will be a non-voting observer on the OpenAI Group PBC Board.

Paul will also join the Safety and Security Committee (SSC) of the Foundation Board, working alongside its chair, Zico Kolter. The SSC provides governance over safety and security practices across all of OpenAI, including OpenAI Group PBC.

Paul brings government experience spanning two administrations through his work at the Center for AI Standards and Innovation ⁠ (opens in a new window) (CAISI) within the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), an agency of the U.S. Department of Commerce, where he is a Senior Tech Advisor 1. During his time at CAISI and its predecessor, the U.S. AI Safety Institute, Paul has worked on evaluating frontier AI models, including capabilities with national security implications, and on approaches to mitigating associated safety and security risks.
points: Paul Christiano joins the OpenAI Foundation Board and its Safety and Security Committee, bringing experience in AI alignment, safety, and standards.

highlights.title: Gurney called up to World Series Finals after withdrawals due to visa issues
highlights.summary: Daryl Gurney has been called up to play at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam after visa issues led to the withdrawal of Philippines players Lourence Ilagan and Alexis Toylo from the September 17-20 event.
body: Northern Ireland's Gurney and the Netherlands' Maik Kuivenhoven were the highest-ranked players on the reserve list and have replaced Ilagan and Toylo respectively after the pair did not receive a decision on their Schengen visa applications before having to travel to China this week for the final two events of the PDC Asian Tour season.
Gurney will face reigning tournament champion and home favourite Michael van Gerwen in the first round at AFAS Live on Thursday September 17, while Kuivenhoven plays Jonny Clayton the following day.
Luke Littler, the 2024 champion who was beaten 11-7 by Van Gerwen in last year's final, heads to Amsterdam aiming to keep his bid for the first-ever clean sweep of majors in one year on track.
Luke Humphries opens against Jermaine Wattimena, while Gian van Veen will face Chris Dobey.

body: Note that these estimates are based on gross revenue from player spending across the App Store and Google Play only. It does not feature estimates from alternative marketplaces or direct-to-consumer platforms.

Aniplex’s long-running gacha Fate/Grand Order has seen player spending spike to its highest monthly sum of the year. The game made $57.7 million this August with an anniversary celebration in Japan, more than doubling July’s $22.5m.

In fact, this was the anime-style RPG’s best month since last August. The game makes 89% of its earnings from Japan, meaning the month is a major one each year - more than the North American anniversary in early July.

On a daily spending basis, earnings reached their highest in more than five years this August. Fate/Grand Order generated $4.6m on the 15th, surpassing any daily record from the past five anniversaries but not quite matching the game’s lifetime high of $5.6m on January 1st, 2021.

highlights.title: ‘Holy Wood Dust’ Review: Victor Kossakovsky’s Soothing, if Slightly Dull, Documentary Will Make You Want to Hug a Tree
highlights.summary: Playing out of competition in Venice, the latest from the 'Gunda' and 'Architecton' helmer is a meditation on the precious beauty and importance of trees.
body: Cinematic lyrical poet Victor Kossakovsky ( Architecton, Gunda ) offers in Holy Wood Dust another distinctive non-fiction meditation on a theme, a work that’s eloquent even if the author’s message is not always explicitly articulated. This time the subject is trees, mostly living ones growing, or at least trying to grow, around the Dolomites in Northern Italy — though the focus broadens to incorporate trees grown on an industrial scale for the Christmas season, especially in Germany.

Things have recently gotten a little spicier and more innovative in the nature documentary space, making this feel a bit old-school compared to, say Jesse McLean’s wonderful Light Needs, an experimental work about indoor plants that literally gives our potted pals voices, or the recent kaleidoscopic crowd-sourced feature Super Nature by Ed Sayers. French doc Heart of an Oak from a few years back, on the other hand, is comparatively less formally innovative, but by focusing on just the one tree and getting stuck right in to how that forms a micro-ecosystem on its own, it feels more cohesive and rich in factoids than the wafty approach allows here.
points: Playing out of competition in Venice, the latest from the 'Gunda' and 'Architecton' helmer is a meditation on the precious beauty and importance of trees.

highlights.title: The quick guide to fall vaccines and when you should get them
highlights.summary: Labor Day is in the rearview mirror, kids are back to school, and a squall of pumpkin spice is upon us. It's that time again to prepare for the equally inevitable respiratory virus season with annual vaccines. With fervent anti-vaccine activist Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
body: Despite all of that, the fall vaccine effort is looking like it will likely be somewhat smooth, potentially unremarkable even. The Food and Drug Administration has approved updated flu and COVID-19 shots for this season. Those shots have already begun arriving at pharmacies —in case your pharmacy hasn’t already sent you multiple texts and reminders. While there are still some snags for access, it seems like it will be a lot like last year’s fall vaccine rollout.

Major insurance plans have agreed to continue covering vaccines previously recommended by the CDC’s advisory panel, including the seasonal ones, at no charge. That agreement runs at least through the end of 2027.
State and local health officials are also expecting a generally normal rollout and are keeping an eye toward improving vaccination rates.

highlights.title: Tongue tears through sorry Pakistan as England earn lead on day one
highlights.summary: England dominated a sorry-looking Pakistan yet again on day one of the third Test at Edgbaston, bowling the tourists out for 133 before closing on 156-4, with a 23-run lead.
body: Emilio Gay (60) and Harry Brook (52no) each struck fifties in the final session to rescue England from 39-3 after their own top-order wobble, in which Joe Root (8) was pinned lbw for a 10th time in 13 innings by Pakistan's hugely-impressive debutant pacer Razaullah (2-42).

Root had earlier opted to insert the visitors at the toss in overcast conditions, but it wasn't long before his side were preparing to bat anyway, as Pakistan lasted just 33.5 overs - their shortest innings in a series full of disappointing batting displays.
Seven wickets fell in a chaotic morning session which saw Ollie Robinson (3-15) claim his 100th in Test cricket, before the innings was wrapped up soon after lunch.

Josh Tongue finished with 4-42, dismantling the stumps of Pakistan captain Babar Azam (7), Mohammad Imran (5) and lone bright spark Saud Shakeel (43), while Jofra Archer proved potent once more, taking 3-25.

highlights.title: Valheim 1.0's Steam player count soars to a huge 5-year high, but it's not enough to beat the viral survival game's early access peak
highlights.summary: The five-year wait for Valheim 1.0 doesn't seem to have hurt the survival game behemoth's popularity all that much. After leaving early access, the crafty viking sim is enjoying a huge resurgence in Steam player numbers.
body: Still, Valheim hasn't been able to capture lightning in a bottle twice. At least, not yet. The game peaked over five years ago when 502,387 people logged on at the same time, aided by memes that sailed across the web and a playerbase that wasn't totally pandemic-free yet.

Today's Steam stats may also be skewed by the fact that Iron Gate's breakout game is now available to play on PS5, Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox Series X/S consoles. The Valheim crowd on Steam no longer represents the entire Valheim crowd, then. We'll see how high those numbers soar as the game heads into its first proper weekend of release.

The Valheim 1.0 update arguably matches the game's incredible launch stats, too. Iron Gate's new patch notes are almost 1,800 words long and include too much new newness for me to neatly summarise here. Long story short, if you've not touched the procgen afterlife in a while, Valheim 1.0 adds a new biome called Deep North, over 40 fresh weapons, lots of new bits and bobs and hammers to craft, a graphics setting to stretch draw distances, and much more.

body: Taking place on September 14th, 2026 in Bratislava, PixelCon is a free, open conference aimed at game developers, students, indie creators and professionals from across the games industry. Registration is required due to limited capacity.

Among the international speakers is Jeremy Widdowson, head of growth at Rovio, bringing experience from one of Europe's best-known mobile games companies, the studio behind the global Angry Birds franchise.

The programme also features Stanislav Stankovič, game design director at Electronic Arts, Maya Hofree, general manager of Hay Day at Supercell, and Florian Blaesche, director of player experience at Wooga, who will share their perspectives on building successful mobile games, player engagement and long-term retention.
The international line-up will be joined by Slovak and Czech industry leaders, including Pixel Federation experts and founders of local studios such as Flyboys, PowerPlay Studio and Impact Games.

highlights.title: I Let an AI Agent Hack All My Gadgets—and I’d Do It Again
highlights.summary: After I removed the safety guardrails from a powerful open-source model, it found vulnerabilities in my household devices and hacked into a PC. But it also told me how to make everything a lot more secure.
body: You’re probably aware that frontier AI models have attained advanced cybersecurity capabilities in recent months. They can find zero-day bugs in large codebases and scan computers for vulnerabilities at lightning speed. To make things even more exciting, cybersecurity agents sometimes go rogue, colluding with one another and hacking into outside systems to gain an edge.

But Will, you might be thinking, giving an impish, all-powerful cybersecurity agent access to your home network is batshit. And you would be correct! Nevertheless, I believe that a good way to understand the cybersecurity hellscape in front of us is to pay it a visit.
I got the idea for the experiment after discovering Abliteration AI, a startup that offers access to powerful AI models with the usual guardrails removed.

Most mainstream AI models will refuse to respond to certain queries, and they will certainly refuse to find and exploit vulnerabilities in computer systems. But it’s possible to remove these restrictions by finding and modifying certain patterns within an open-weight model’s internal parameters. You can tweak the patterns that lead to refusals through a process known as abliteration.
points: After I removed the safety guardrails from a powerful open-source model, it found vulnerabilities in my household devices and hacked into a PC.
But it also told me how to make everything a lot more secure.

highlights.title: A Stealth Startup Thinks It Just Hacked the Memory Shortage
highlights.summary: Kepler Computing claims a new approach to chip design—and a proprietary material—can help end the supply bottlenecks that have sent memory prices surging.
body: An ambitious chip startup that has spent more than seven years quietly trying to redesign the architecture for computer memory has just come out of stealth mode and believes its new approach can help ease the global memory-chip shortage —provided it can produce its technology at scale.

Kepler Computing, a San Jose, California–based startup founded in 2018 by a team of physicists and computer scientists, says it has developed a new architecture for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) that directly addresses some of the chip supply bottlenecks that are constraining the computing market.

While chipmakers typically rely on expensive extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUV) to shrink the transistors on a chip, thereby packing more technology into the same amount of space, Kepler claims that its “3D stacking” approach and a proprietary new material allow it to increase density without relying on EUV at all—and it can work with existing semiconductor fabrication plants.

highlights.title: Apple unveils folding iPhone Duo as new CEO takes center stage
highlights.summary: The passport-size iPhone Duo serves as the first big test for John Ternus, who took over for Tim Cook last week. Apple has unveiled the iPhone Duo, the company’s first foldable phone and the most significant change to the iPhone since the smartphone’s introduction in 2007.
body: The nearly $2,000 device takes inspiration from Apple iPads and combines it with the portability and features of iPhones. When opened, it is the company’s largest phone display and Apple’s thinnest iPhone.

“iPhone Duo brings an entirely new design while preserving everything you love from an iPhone,” John Ternus, the company’s new chief executive said. “It feels effortless to use and it makes new experiences possible.”
The Duo opens and closes like a passport to double its screen size.

“I started the day with an intelligent personal hub and why there’s no product in the world that is better to be that hub than iPhone,” Ternus said. “We think the best way to achieve that is with a foldable design. Others have created foldables that just feel like two phones stuck together … scrolling through vertical content feels compromised. We started with the experience that we wanted for ourselves, a larger display that feels as natural and intuitive as an iPad … the result is a series of remarkable innovations that we believe will redefine the experience of using a foldable phone.”

highlights.title: Students who use AI generally score worse at school
highlights.summary: Students who use AI to help them study tend to perform worse at school than those who don't, according to data from a global OECD educational report. The situation is more complex than it sounds though, with certain types of AI use giving learners a slight boost, especially among students taught to…
body: But AI use combined with training to assess its results can give test scores a boost.

The OECD’s Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) takes data from countries around the world every few years. This year’s study, based on data collected in 2025, is the first to be carried out since AI use went truly mainstream. It tests 15-year-old students in science, math, and reading, and draws from over 760,000 students in 91 countries.

After adjusting for socioeconomic status, students who never use AI generally outperformed those who do in science. How stark the difference is varies though: Students who used AI for specific tasks like summarizing texts they were meant to read, or drafting writing assignments, performed relatively worse, while those who used it for preliminary research or more broadly to “help me learn” saw less of a performance drop.
Frequency of use has an impact too: Those who only used AI once or twice a year and those who used it daily tended to perform the worst, with better results for monthly or weekly AI users.
points: Students who use AI to help them study tend to perform worse at school than those who don't, according to data from a global OECD educational report.
But AI use combined with training to assess its results can give test scores a boost.
This year’s study, based on data collected in 2025, is the first to be carried out since AI use went truly mainstream.
It tests 15-year-old students in science, math, and reading, and draws from over 760,000 students in 91 countries.

body: In fact, Liang’s silhouette had gotten so muscular that her stunt double couldn’t convincingly pull off her physique for action sequences — so she had to wear butt pads to make her glutes match the results of Chun-Li’s rigorous squat routine.

“I knew it was serious when we were filming a scene kind of later in the movie, and I saw Callina’s stunt double, and I was like, ‘What are you wearing?’ And there were like these butt pads that she had to wear just to match Callina’s physique,” Sakurai said.
Noah Centineo, who plays Ken Masters, chimed in: “Yeah, and then we had to wear them out of solidarity, too.”
Liang has been open about the work it took to bring Chun-Li to life, saying she took on a grueling martial arts routine and even ate a dozen eggs every single day to gain enough muscle mass.

highlights.title: ‘I’m sick of her talking about it’: 11 readers share how GLP-1s have affected their relationships
highlights.summary: As weight loss drugs have risen all around the world, it has reshaped users’ relationships for better and for worse. As GLP-1 use continues to rise in the US and the UK, people’s bodies are being reshaped – as are their relationships.
body: “Relationships tend to develop a sense of equilibrium and predictability over time,” says Dr Lindsey Berisha, a licensed clinical psychologist who has worked with clients using GLP-1s for over 10 years. “When one partner undergoes a significant change, it can shift that equilibrium, and even positive change can create uncertainty for both partners.”

Berisha says that her clients who use GLP-1s often report feeling relieved that they are no longer consumed with thoughts of food. These users often develop more self-compassion, she says, as they realize what they previously interpreted as a failure or lack of self-control was a legitimate biological drive and food preoccupation that made life harder for them. “This shift can often be more impactful than the weight loss itself,” she says.

But these changes can elicit mixed reactions from partners, family and friends, says psychologist Dr Rachel Goldman, ranging “from being supportive to feeling insecure, left behind, or worried that the relationship itself is changing”.

highlights.title: Beloved Fantasy Book Series Redfall Officially Returns in 2027
highlights.summary: For 25 years from 1986 to 2011, writer Brian Jacques stole the hearts of readers everywhere with his Redwall series of fantasy novels. The Rogue Crew was released in 2011, three months after Jacques' death, and for 15 years it has remained the final entry in the series — until now.
body: As spotted by the Redwall fan wiki, a 23rd book in the series has been announced, and it's coming next year. The book, titled Orphans of Mossflower, will be released on Sept. 7, 2027, alongside a new boxed set containing the other 22 novels in the series. Both coincide with the 40th anniversary of the series, which was first published in the U.K. in 1986 and in the United States a year later. While details are sparse, Orphans of Mossflower is being advertised as being written by Jacques.

Fans have suspected a 23rd book in the series existed in some form for over a decade. In 2010, publisher Penguin held a contest that let one lucky fan name a character in the next Redwall novel. The winner came forward in 2015 with details on the character, and fans realized they did not appear in The Rogue Crew, fueling the theory that another book existed.

highlights.title: Apple brought ceramic back for the Series 12
highlights.summary: The Apple Watch Series 12 is launching with a ceramic option, making it the company's first wearable since 2019's Series 5 that can be configured with the pricey, scratch-resistant material.
body: Apple is bringing back its pricier, more durable option. It should be more scratch-resistant than titanium.

While Apple didn’t resurrect its “Apple Watch Edition” branding for the Series 12 (it stopped using the name in a forward-facing manner when the Series 4 launched), the new ceramic option is similarly made for high rollers who won’t mind shelling out far more than the Series 12’s $399 starting price.

It’s interesting to look back at Apple’s history of high-end case material options. While it started with an 18-karat rose or yellow gold case option for the first Apple Watch, the company switched to ceramic as its premium option for the Series 2, 3, and 5. Since 2019, each launch has offered aluminum as the most affordable option, plus either stainless steel or titanium (sometimes both) as pricier alternatives.

highlights.title: Newly Discovered Plant-Eating Insects Named After Taylor Swift
highlights.summary: Taylor Swift, the award-winning billionaire singer and songwriter, is getting a new honor: The megastar is the namesake of several recently discovered species of plant-feeding insects from Australia.
body: The Swiftiephylus insects are closely associated with Australian she-oaks, trees and shrubs adapted to environments ranging from tropical forests to coastal dunes and extreme heat, according to UC Riverside. Many plant bugs spend their entire lives on a particular host plant, from hatching through adulthood and egg laying.

UC Riverside entomology doctoral student Sarah Schroeder decided to name the insects after Swift, in the hopes her association with the bugs will elevate both the insects and the concept of insect conservation more generally. “It felt authentic to me as a lifelong Swiftie to honor Taylor in this way, as well as bring attention to the diversity of insects that has yet to be discovered,” Schroeder said in a statement provided by the university.

highlights.summary: From indoor scent training to the longest-lasting slow feeders, these are experts’ top recommendations for keeping dogs fulfilled. The best toys and tools in the US for bored indoor cats. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: A dog is much more than just a pet. They’re like family, the most eager companions for your big adventures and then the best accompaniment for an evening of snuggling up on the couch and whittling away at your Netflix queue.

At least, that’s the ideal situation. In the real world, a dog who gets too little attention and exercise or, on the flip side, is over-stimulated or over-tired, can be a real problem. There are lots of warning signs, such as a dog that is overly antsy or destructive, but Suzanne Clothier, an expert dog trainer and author of numerous books on dog enrichment, sums it up in a very simple way: “Can you watch TV or read a book in peace? If not, the dog’s telling you something.”

While there’s no one-button fix for a bored dog, advancements in enrichment toys and training are making it easier to give your little pal a fulfilled life. We spoke with five certified dog experts to get their favorite tips, tricks, toys and techniques to bolster your best buddy’s confidence and attitude.

Flare delivers high quality images over 50% faster. Both support transparent backgrounds for assets ranging from infographics to games.
body: Available now in the API.
